copy of the character ROM, made at start-up by $81CA

sprite shapes expanded at start-up by $8243 from $82B8

comments.text: The 6510's data direction register for $01; the game leaves it as the KERNAL set it.
The processor port: $3D in play (BASIC and KERNAL ROMs out, the RAM KERNAL copy and I/O in), set by the loader at $C000; $81CA banks the character ROM in for its copy and puts the old value back.

Pointer used by many routines in turn: the clear at start-up, the character-ROM copy, the sprite expansion, the bitmap clear, the text printer, Jumpman's materialising, the header copy, the game over and the ending banner. Low byte.
High byte of the pointer at $20.

Second pointer, the source beside $20's destination: the character-ROM copy, the sprite expansion, the text printer, the letter shape ($8D79), Jumpman's materialising and the high-score moves. Low byte.

High byte of the pointer at $2A.

Level 9: the high byte of that offset.

Level 9: the high byte of the times-8 half.

Scratch byte: shifts in the note table, the sprite expansion and the letter shape; the bonus count, the game over, level 8's pointer Y, level 9's bomb number and the ending banner.

Scratch byte: the title's colour cycle and player count, new life's bullet count, the bonus count and the bomb check's cell code.

Sprite 2's in-use byte (level 11's hatchling).

Sprite 1's X, low byte.

The base of the collision bytes the interrupt writes each frame: $90+n is $D01E (sprite with sprite) when sprite n took part, else 0.
Sprite 0's collisions with other sprites, $D01E when Jumpman touched something, else 0: the touch checks and level 3's ladders read it.
The KERNAL's STOP-key flag, used only by the RAM copy of the KERNAL's own keyboard scan.
The base of the background collision bytes: $98+n is $D01F when sprite n touched the picture, else 0.
Sprite 0's background collisions; level 4 reads $98+n for its stones.
Counts 0, 1 on each run tick: Jumpman's two-step animations.
Counts 0 to 3 on each run tick: four-step animations, also used by levels 4, 11 and 12.
Set for the one frame on which the run speed's counter comes round: Jumpman moves only then.
Set for the one frame on which the enemy speed's counter comes round.
Jumpman's state: 0 alive, 1 hit (set by a touch check or a fall), 2 dying; play_level takes a life when it returns to 0 after 2.
Cleared by the loader ($C000); the check between turns ($9974) locks the machine up if $B2 and $B3 add up to $3F.
Cleared by the loader; the other half of the check between turns.
The KERNAL's last-key byte: the game's keyboard hook ($823E) copies the key now down into it, and the interrupt reads it.
The KERNAL's count of keys in its buffer, written by its own keyboard scan; the game reads keys through $C5.
The KERNAL's key now down (its matrix code), copied to $C5 by the game's keyboard hook ($823E).
The KERNAL's keyboard table pointer, low byte, used only by its own scan.
The KERNAL's keyboard table pointer, high byte.
The loader's copy pointer at $C000, low byte.
The loader's copy pointer, high byte: $E0 to $FF.
The KERNAL's keyboard buffer, ten bytes, filled by its own scan; the game never reads it, which is why typing into the buffer does nothing.
The KERNAL's keyboard buffer size, read by its own scan.
The KERNAL's key-repeat delay count, used by its own scan.
The KERNAL's key-repeat speed count.
The KERNAL's SHIFT, CTRL and Commodore key flags.
The KERNAL's previous SHIFT flags.
The KERNAL's keyboard decode vector, pointed at the game's hook $823E by the cold start.
High byte of the keyboard decode vector.
The KERNAL's PAL/NTSC flag, read by its own code in the RAM copy.
The IRQ vector, pointed at the game's interrupt $863C by the cold start.
High byte of the IRQ vector.
The NMI vector, pointed at $8009 by the cold start, so the RESTORE key starts the game again.
High byte of the NMI vector.
The base of the levels' own variables, $0880-$08FF, cleared at the start of each turn; level 3 reads its ladder steps as $087F+X for X 1 to 6.

A level's first variable: level 3's first ladder step; level 4's stone flags ($0880+n); level 6's wall count; level 7's bullet states; level 8's letter count; level 9's used-bomb flags; level 10's frame count; level 11's hatching count; level 12's gust flag. At start-up also the note table's source.
A level's second variable: level 3's ladder step; level 8's next letter's Y; level 10's place number; level 12's gust's voice.
Level 3's third ladder step; level 12's gust strength.
Level 3's fourth ladder step (the first going up).
Level 3's fifth ladder step; level 8's colour task's count.
Level 3's sixth ladder step.
$0888+n: level 4's bounce step; level 6's wall step, low byte; level 7's sideways sway count.
$0890+n: level 4's bounce X step; level 6's wall step, high byte; level 7's up-and-down sway count; level 8's letters, in the order they stand.
$0898+n: level 4's bounce X step, high byte.
Level 6: the Y of the next wall.
The base of $08C0-$08FF, cleared at each turn: level 8's letter script is copied to $08C0 from $08BF+X.
Level 3: held while its bomb routine turns the ladders, so the ladder task skips; level 8: the start of its letter script.
Level 8: the letter script's Y byte, set before each letter is drawn.
The last byte the cold start clears in its first loop.

The task list: 16 addresses, two bytes each, called every frame by the interrupt ($87D3) when not 0. Slot 0 Jumpman, 1 his death, 2 the bullets, 3 the sprite writer, 4 to 7 the level's or screen's own tasks, 13 the status bar, 14 the sound, 15 the random numbers.
The first task's high byte; the dispatcher reads $0900,X and $0901,X.
The base the interrupt writes new tasks through: $0906+X for X 2 to 8 reaches slots 4 to 7 at $0908-$090F.
The high-byte base for the same writes.
The task dispatcher's place in the list, stepping by 2.
Counts frames; its low bits give $09BF and $09BE, and the title, intro and ending use it for every-other-frame work.
A second frame count, reset by the title and the ending to time things in 16-frame steps.
Frames counted for wait_frames ($8D0F).
Counts frames up to the run speed ($09B6); when it gets there $A2 is set and it starts again.
Counts frames up to the enemy speed ($09B7), for $A3 and $09D3.
The step of the jump Jumpman is in, 0 when he is not jumping.
The stick's X: -1 left, 0, 1 right ($FF, 0, 1), from the direction table at $8845.
The stick's Y: -1 up, 0, 1 down, from the table at $8855.
The stick's four direction bits, 0 when pushed.
The recorded input that replaces the stick when not 0 (set to 0 for each level).
The fire button: 0 while it is pressed.
How fire is read: 0 from the port, 1 never pressed, anything else always pressed.
The sprites' width doubling, written to $D01D each frame.
The sprites' height doubling, written to $D017 each frame: levels 3 and 6 set it.
Set to ask the interrupt to show the text screen at the next frame ($8B97).
Set to ask the interrupt to show the bitmap at the next frame ($8B9B).
Four new tasks waiting to go into slots 4 to 7 ($0938-$093F), installed by the interrupt at the next frame.
The first waiting task's high byte.
The second waiting task, low byte.
The second waiting task, high byte.
Sound voice 1's record (7 bytes): priority, note time left, release time, waveform, a spare byte, script address. Level 12 reads a gust voice's priority here.
Voice 1's note time left.
Voice 1's release time.
Voice 1's waveform.
Voice 1's script address, low byte.
Voice 1's script address, high byte.
Sound voice 3's record; the level's end waits on its priority.
Held by the sound starters while they change a voice's record, so the sound task skips that frame.
Jumpman's death: set once his falling shape and the death sound have been started.
Jumpman's death: set once the death tune has been started.
The base of the last Y written to each sprite: the sprite task writes the Y register only when $098F+n has changed.
The colours under Jumpman's body, from the floor probe ($97A8): bit 1 colour 1 (bombs), bit 2 colour 2 (girders, slopes and up-ropes), bit 3 colour 3 (ladders and down-ropes); ORed with $09D1.
The colours in the line under Jumpman's feet, the same bits; ORed with $09D2.
The level being played, 0 to 11; $FF before the first.
The player whose turn it is, 0 to 3.
The number of players less one, chosen on the title.
The highest player still in the game.
A JSR and RTS built here by the cold start: the task dispatcher writes each task's address into it.
The task trampoline's address, low byte, rewritten for each task.
The task trampoline's address, high byte.
The RTS of the first trampoline: the empty routine whose address fills unused routine slots in the headers and task list.
A second JSR and RTS: a routine's address is written into $09B3/$09B4 and called here (the header's routines, IOINIT).
The second trampoline's address, low byte, set before each call of a header routine.
The second trampoline's address, high byte.
The second trampoline's RTS.
The run speed, 1 (fastest) to 8, from the player's record; 9 stops everything.
The enemies' speed, set with Jumpman's at each new life.
The sprite enable bits the sprite task builds and writes to $D015.
The sprites' X high bits the sprite task builds and writes to $D010.
The number printer's flag: 0 while only zeros have been printed, so they become spaces.
The last key the interrupt saw, so a held key counts once.
Set while the time bonus counts down.
Frames until the next bonus tick.
The frame count modulo 4.
The frame count modulo 8.
Set while the bitmap is on screen: the status task only draws then.
The digit key pressed, 1 to 9 (from the table at $8864), 0 when none.
Set when nobody has a Jumpman left: the next turn goes back to the cold start.
Set when the last player has had a turn: the next turn moves to the next level.
Set on the title once the number of players has been chosen; until then the title task keeps the title tune going.
Set once level 12 has been played: from then on levels are drawn at random.
Set to 0 when a turn's set-up begins and to 1 once its sprites are placed; nothing reads it.
The step of Jumpman's death bounce, through the table at $A5E8.
The death bounce's X step, low byte.
The death bounce's X step, high byte; the cold start also writes $09C9-$09D0 there, the bomb wiper's script (blank shape, X, Y, 1).
The X in the bomb wiper's script, set by the bomb check (and level 9) before it runs.
The Y in the bomb wiper's script.
Extra colour bits ORed into the body probe: level 3 sets bit 3 while Jumpman touches a moving ladder.
Extra colour bits ORed into the feet probe.
Set for the frame on which the enemies move (the enemy count came round and Jumpman is not dying): every level's moving thing waits for it.
The four players' records, 8 bytes each: score (3 bytes), next extra life (3 bytes), run speed and lives ($FF when out).
The first player's run speed; the title writes $0A06 + 8 × player.
The first player's lives; $FF means the player is out.
The byte before the current player's record, read by the score check as $0A27+X.
The current player's score, low byte, copied in from the record at each turn.
The current score, middle byte.
The current score, high byte.
The score at which the current player's next Jumpman comes, low byte (first 7,500).
The next life's score, middle byte.
The next life's score, high byte.
The current player's run speed.
The current player's Jumpmen left.
$0A30+n: each bullet's X step, low byte; level 7 sways it.
$0A38+n: each bullet's X step, high byte.
$0A40+n: each bullet's Y step.
The byte before the header in use: the turn's start copies $0C3F+X to $0BFF+X for X 1 to 64.
The level header in use, copied from $0C40 at each turn: the level number's two digits.
The level number's second digit, written into the status bar.
Bombs left on the level; the level ends when it reaches 0.
How many bullets at a time.
Jumpman's start, X low byte.
Jumpman's start, X high byte.
Jumpman's start, Y.
The offset added to Jumpman's X before it becomes a bomb cell code.
The offset added to Jumpman's Y before it becomes a bomb cell code.
Points for each bomb, 100 on every level.
The time bonus, low byte, counted down during play.
The time bonus, high byte.
The byte after the bonus; the level's end adds the carry into it.
The level's sprite set-up list, low byte.
High byte of the header's sprite set-up list, copied to $57 at each turn.
The bomb positions, low byte.
The bomb positions, high byte.
The bomb list, low byte.
The bomb list, high byte.

The change scripts' list, high byte.

The bomb routines' list, high byte.

The routine run for every bomb, high byte.

The start routine, high byte.

The end routine, high byte.
The byte before the ladder positions: the ladder check reads $0C31+Y for Y 1 to 8.
The byte before the rope positions: the rope check compares with $0C39+Y for Y 1 to 6.
The byte before the stored header: the turn's start reads $0C3F+X.
The level's header as copied from $BC00 at the level's start, kept unchanged for each turn's fresh copy at $0C00.
The stored header's draw script, low byte.
The stored header's draw script, high byte.
The stored header's border colour.
The byte before the status bar text: the clear and the template copy write $3DFF+X for X 1 to 80.

The status bar's 80 characters, two rows of 40, copied into the bitmap by the status task: JUMPMEN = 00, LEVEL 00 and RUN SPEED 00 on the first row, SCORE, PLAYER and BONUS on the second. Written here, then drawn when it changes.
The tens digit of JUMPMEN in the status bar.
The units digit of JUMPMEN.
The status bar's first row from the 15th character: the level's end writes its message here.
The tens digit of LEVEL in the status bar.
The units digit of LEVEL.
The run speed's digit in the status bar.
The player's number in the status bar.
The byte before the copy at $3E80; the bitmap clear empties $3E80-$3ECF through it.
The status bar as last drawn: the status task draws only the characters that differ from it.
Level 8's letter, built by $8D79 as a shape for the shape drawer: for each of 8 rows, 8, 0 and the row, then 8 pixels.
The letter shape's first row's X offset, 0.
The letter shape's first row's Y offset, then the first row's pixels.
The high-score table, 20 lines of 16 screen codes. The cold start fills it only when it does not begin with "0", so the scores outlast a restart by RESTORE.
The cartridge's header: cold-start and warm-start vectors, both $8009, then the signature CBM80 that makes the KERNAL's reset jump through them. On this disk the loader jumps to $8009 itself.

The cartridge signature CBM80. Level 10's bomb routine stores A there ($B754), 0 after a sound has started: on the cartridge the store did nothing, but on this disk, where the image is RAM, it breaks the signature.

Start of the game, entered once from the loader (and again by the RESTORE key, through the NMI vector this routine sets). Silences the SID, resets the stack, hides the sprites, clears $0400-$79FF, sets up the sprite shapes ($8243), the bitmap row tables at $1000/$1100, the JSR trampolines at $09AE and $09B2, the note table at $1200, the colour-set table at $1400, the high-score table at $7E00 (only when it does not already start with "0", so scores survive a restart), the task list at $0900, calls the KERNAL's IOINIT, points the IRQ at $863C and the NMI at $8009, and goes to the title at $958D.
The colours: $8B6B fills the text screen's colour RAM.

Build the bitmap's row tables: for each of the 200 pixel lines, the address of its first byte in the bitmap at $4000, low bytes at $1000 and high bytes at $1100 (8 lines to a character row, 320 bytes to a row).
Turn $09AE and $09B2 into JSR $xxxx / RTS: the task dispatcher at $87D6 and the IOINIT call at $8175 write the target into each.
Copy the twelve note frequencies at $81FA to $0880, then double them seven times into $1200: 96 frequencies, 8 octaves of 12 semitones, low byte first.
Run speed 9 (the title's own) into $09B6, $58 and $59.

Build the colour-set table at $1400: for each byte value, a bit for each of the four multicolour pixel values (0-3) that appears in the byte. The movement code reads a bitmap byte through it to ask "is there floor, ladder or rope colour here".
Seven start values for $09CA-$09D0 from $8237.
The high-score table at $7E00: 20 lines of 16 screen codes, "01." to "20." and spaces. Built only when $7E00 does not hold "0" already.
The task list: 16 address slots at $0900-$091F from $8212. The interrupt calls every slot that is not zero each frame ($87D6).

Find IOINIT without naming its address: read the KERNAL's reset vector at $FFFC, add $11 to reach the operand of its JSR IOINIT, put that address into the trampoline at $09B2 and call it. The loader's patch at $FDD6 makes IOINIT keep the RAM copy of the KERNAL banked in.
Interrupt vectors: IRQ ($0314) to $863C, NMI ($0318) to $8009, so RESTORE restarts the game. Raster interrupt on, at line $E8.
The KERNAL's keyboard decode vector ($028F) to $823E, which keeps only the matrix code of the key pressed.
Copy the character ROM into RAM at $2000 ($81CA), set the volume to 15, sprite multicolour on for all eight sprites with shared colours white and purple, and start the title.
Copy the 2 KB character ROM ($D000-$D7FF) to $2000-$27FF, with CHAREN cleared in $01 for the copy, then enable interrupts. The bitmap text routines draw their letters from this copy.
The byte before the note frequencies: the start-up copy reads $81F9+X for X 1 to 24.
Twelve SID frequencies for one octave, C to B, a semitone apart (each about 1.0595 times the last): the bottom octave of the note table $808A builds at $1200.
The byte before the starting task list: the start-up copy reads $8211+X for X 1 to 32.

The task list as the game starts, copied to $0900: slot 0 $A23A, slot 1 $A4C0, slot 2 $A0F1, slot 3 $887A (the sprite writer), slots 4-12 empty, slot 13 $9F0C, slot 14 $88F2 (sound), slot 15 $8D3D (random number).
The bit for each multicolour pixel value 0-3, used by $80C4 to build the colour-set table.
Start values: $8237-$823D are copied to $09CA-$09D0 at start-up ($80F1); $8236 itself is not copied.
The game's own keyboard decode, called by the KERNAL's SCNKEY through $028F: copies the matrix code of the key now down ($CB) to $C5 and returns, so the KERNAL's buffer and repeat logic never run.

Expand the 45 packed sprite shapes at $82B8 (20 bytes each: 10 rows of 2 bytes) into sprite blocks at $6400, 3 bytes to a row with the third left empty, one block of 64 bytes each (pointers $90-$BC in bank 1); then copy $6400-$7FFF to $2800 for the title screen's bank.

45 multicolour sprite shapes of 8 wide pixels by 10 rows, two bytes a row, expanded by $8243. The sprites point at them as $90 onward; which is which is chosen by the code that sets each sprite's pointer.

The raster interrupt, once a frame at line $E8 (232), entered through the RAM KERNAL's $FF48 and $0314. A timer interrupt (the CIA's, which the KERNAL leaves running) only acknowledges $DC0D and returns. Otherwise: switches the screen between the text screen (bank 0, $D018 $15) and the bitmap (bank 1, screen $6000, bitmap $4000, $D018 $80) when $0936 or $0937 asks; reads the joystick in port 2 (or the demo's input in $0930) into $092F with its X and Y step from $8845/$8855 into $092D/$092E and the fire button into $0931; counts the frame timers $0921-$0925; turns the run-speed timer $0924 against $09B6 into the movement ticks $A2/$A0/$A1 and the enemy timer $0925 against $09B7 into $A3; copies sprite expansion and priority from $0934/$0935; latches the two collision registers per sprite into $90-$97 (sprite with sprite) and $98-$9F (sprite with background); counts down the bonus every $09BD frames ($881E); updates the stars or flashes ($97A8); waits for line $32 to set multicolour again when the bitmap is shown; turns the key now down ($C5) into a digit 1-9 in $09C1 through $8864; installs the task addresses waiting in $0938-$093F into task slots 4-7 ($0908-$090F); calls every task in the list $0900-$091F through the trampoline at $09AE; then sets the next interrupt at line $E8, acknowledges it, calls the KERNAL's SCNKEY and leaves through $8643.
$0936 set: show the text screen. Bank 0, screen $0400 with the character ROM's upper-case set, which the VIC-II sees at $1000 in bank 0 ($D018 $15), bitmap and multicolour off.

$09C0 or $0937 set: show the bitmap. Bank 1, screen $6000, bitmap $4000 ($D018 $80), bitmap mode on; multicolour comes back at line $32 (below, $878A), so the status bar drawn at the bottom of the last frame stays hires.

The stick: port 2 ($DC00), or the recorded input in $0930 when it is not zero. $092F holds the four direction bits (0 when pushed), $092D the X step (-1, 0 or 1) and $092E the Y step, both looked up by those bits.
The fire button into $0931: from the port when $0932 is 0, held down when $0932 is 1, released for any other value.
Five frame counters, $0921-$0925, counted up every frame.

Run speed: when $0924 reaches the speed in $09B6 (1 fastest to 8 slowest; 9 stops it), it is cleared and $A2 is set for this frame, and $A0 (0-1) and $A1 (0-3) step on: the moving routines act only on frames with $A2 set. The same for the enemies with $09B7, $0925 and $A3; $09D3 counts enemy ticks while Jumpman is not dying ($A4 not 2).
Sprite size and priority from their shadows; then each sprite's collision bits: $90+n is $D01E (sprite with sprite) and $98+n $D01F (sprite with background) when sprite n took part, else 0.
$09BF and $09BE: the frame count modulo 8 and 4, for animations.
The time bonus: while $09BC is set, $881E runs every time $09BD counts down to 0.
With the bitmap showing, wait for line $32 and turn multicolour back on.
The keyboard: when the key down changes, find it among the digit keys at $8864 and keep its value 1-9 in $09C1 (0 for none).
Install the tasks asked for since the last frame: each pair at $0938-$093F whose high byte is not zero goes into task slots 4-7 ($0908-$090F) and is cleared.
Call each of the 16 task slots at $0900-$091F that holds an address, through the JSR at $09AE.
Next interrupt at line $E8 again, acknowledge it, set CIA 1's ports for the keyboard and call the KERNAL's SCNKEY ($FF9F), which reaches the game's own decode at $823E.
One step of the time bonus: unless it is already 0, take 100 from the bonus at $0C12/$0C13, play the tick sound at $886E and redraw the bonus on the status bar ($A04E).
The X step for each value of the joystick's four direction bits (0 = pushed): 1 right, -1 ($FF) left, 0 otherwise.
The Y step for each value of the four direction bits: 1 down, -1 up, 0 otherwise.
The keyboard matrix codes of the keys 1 to 9 (index 1-9; the first byte is a placeholder): what $879E compares the key down with to give $09C1.
The sound of a bonus tick, a sound script for $88F2: waveform and release ($FC), envelope ($FE), one note, end ($FF).

Task: write the eight sprites from their shadows. For each sprite n with $67+n set: enable bit in $09B8, pointer from $87+n into $63F8, Y from $7F+n (only when it changed, remembered at $0990), X low from $6F+n, X high from $77+n into $09B9; sprites with $67+n clear are switched off. Then $D010 and $D015 from $09B9 and $09B8.
The jump's high byte, $88; the clearing masks are read from this address as $88E1+X, so X 1 reaches $88E2.
The AND masks that clear sprite n's bit in the enable and X high bits: FE, FD and so on to 7F, read as $88E1+X for X 1 to 8.
The last of the clearing masks, 7F for sprite 7; the setting masks are read from this address as $88E9+X.
The OR masks that set sprite n's bit: 01, 02 and so on to 80, read as $88E9+X for X 1 to 8.

Task: the sound player, three voices, a 7-byte record each at $0940, $0947 and $094E: priority (0 = idle), note time left, the time at which to release the gate, the waveform, a spare byte, and the address of the voice's script. Skipped while $0955 says a new sound is being started. $5F is left holding the OR of the three priorities, so it is 0 only when all three voices are silent. A voice whose note time runs out reads its script: a byte below $FC is a note (index into the frequencies at $1200) followed by its length; $FC sets the waveform and the release time, $FD the pulse width, $FE attack/decay and sustain/release, $FF ends the sound.
Start the sound whose script is at ($38), with priority A, unless another start is pending in $3A/$3B.

Give the sound at ($3A) to a voice with priority A: an idle voice if there is one, else the first voice playing something of lower priority; if every voice is busy with something more important the sound is dropped. $0955 keeps the player out while the record is written.

Draw a level's picture from a drawing script at ($3D): $FE and an address picks the shape ($41); $FD and two bytes set the step between copies ($47, $48); $FF ends; any other byte is X, then Y and a count, and the shape is drawn that many times, moved by the step each time.

Draw one shape at X $43, Y $44 into the multicolour bitmap: records of four bytes, a run length, an X and a Y offset and a colour (0-3), ending with a 0. Each record sets a horizontal run of that many wide pixels to the colour, through the row table at $1000/$1100 and the masks at $8B0C/$8B1C.
AND masks that keep the other three pixels of a multicolour byte, for pixel 0-3, repeated for each colour.
OR masks that put colour 0-3 (rows of four) into pixel 0-3 of a multicolour byte.
Clear the bitmap's screen at $6000, its colour RAM and the bitmap $4000-$5FFF, set the sprite pointers to $90 ($8C06), and clear the status bar text at $3E80-$3ECF.
Clear the text screen at $0400 to spaces and its colour RAM to black, sprite pointers to $20.
Ask the interrupt to show the text screen at the next frame ($0936).
Ask the interrupt to show the bitmap at the next frame ($0937).
Stop all three voices: clear each record and its gate, and the flags $0955, $5F and $3B.
Blank the screen (clear $D011 bit 4).
Show the screen again (set $D011 bit 4).

Colour the bitmap for a level: screen $6000 all $85 (colours 8 and 5, orange and green), colour RAM all 6 (blue), background black; sprite pointers to $90, and the bottom two rows of the screen cleared to 0 for the status bar.
Point all eight sprites of the bitmap screen at shape $90.
Write the 24-bit number at $4E-$50 as six screen-code digits at ($4C), by repeated subtraction of the powers of ten at $8DD0; leading zeros become spaces except the last digit.
Mark all eight sprites unused ($67+n), clear the sprite-background priority, expansion and $0C0B and $09BD; all sprites multicolour.
Stop the action: run speed 9 (nothing moves), empty task slots 4-7 ($8D62), the sprites ($8C76) and the sound ($8B9F).
Copy X characters from ($51) to the text screen at column $53, row $54, and colour them $55.
Read sprite set-ups from a list at ($56): sprite number, X low, X high, Y, pointer, colour, repeated until $FF; each fills the sprite's shadows and marks it used.
Wait A frames, counted by the interrupt in $0923.
Print text line A (an offset into the table at $8DE2, 6 bytes a line) on the text screen ($8CA2).
Task, and called: an 16-bit shift register at $58/$59 stepped eight times, the new bit the exclusive OR of bits 3 and 0 of $59 (a linear feedback generator). Returns the low byte.
Empty task slots 4-7: put the address of the RTS at $09B1 into each of the four pairs at $0938-$093F, which the interrupt then installs, and clear $09D1/$09D2.

Turn character A of the RAM character set at $2000 into a shape at $7900 for the shape drawer ($8A91): for each of its 8 rows, 8 pixels, 0 and the row number, then the row's pixels in colour 3 or 0. Used only by level 8, for the letters.
100000, 10000, 1000, 100, 10 and 1, three bytes each low first: the subtractions of $8C11.
The middle bytes of the powers of ten, read as $8DD1+X.
The high bytes of the powers of ten, read as $8DD2+X.

The text screen's 16 lines, 6 bytes each (column, row, colour, address and length of the screen codes), printed by $8D1C with the line's offset: 0 EPYX, 6 PRESENTS, 12 and 24 the rainbow bars, 18 JUMPMAN JUNIOR, 30 (C) 1983 BY EPYX, 36 a blank line, 42 DESIGNED BY RANDY GLOVER, 48 the green bar, 54 NUMBER OF PLAYERS, 60-78 the four PLAYER # SPEED prompts, 84 TOTAL SCORE:, 90 ***HIGH SCORES.***.
The text lines' second field, the row, read as $8DE3+X.
The text lines' third field, the colour.
The text lines' fourth field, the address of the screen codes, low byte.
The text lines' fifth field, the address's high byte.
The text lines' sixth field, the length.
The rest of the text-line table, from the middle of line 11 to the end of line 15 (the high-score screen's lines), beyond the reach of the field labels above.

The title screen's text in screen codes, read through the line table at $8DE2: EPYX, PRESENTS, 18 reversed spaces for the rainbow bars, JUMPMAN JUNIOR in reverse, (C) 1983 BY EPYX, a blank line, DESIGNED BY RANDY GLOVER, 40 reversed spaces for the green bar, NUMBER OF PLAYERS (1-4) ?, PLAYER #2 SPEED (1-8) ? (the 2 is changed for each player), TOTAL SCORE: and ***HIGH SCORES.***.

The girder shape, 4 double-width pixels by 6 lines in colour 2 (green): solid top and bottom rows with a lattice between. Drawn in runs by the draw scripts, stepping 4 across, or 4 across and 2 up or down for a slope.
The girder eraser: the girder shape with every pixel 0. Change scripts draw it to take girders away; the bomb wiper ($09CA) uses it on a defused bomb.
The ladder shape, 8 double-width pixels by 8 lines in colour 3 (blue): two rails and a rung. Drawn in columns stepping 8 down.
The ladder eraser: the ladder shape with every pixel 0, used by change scripts to take ladder sections away.
The bomb shape, 4 double-width pixels by 6 lines in colour 1 (orange): the floor probe finds bombs by that colour.
The up-rope shape, 2 double-width pixels by 8 lines in colour 2 (green), a zig-zag strand: Jumpman is carried up it because colour 2 in his body lifts him.
The down-rope shape, 2 double-width pixels by 8 lines in colour 3 (blue): at a rope position of the header Jumpman slides down it.
The rope eraser: the rope shape with every pixel 0.
Start tune A, an offset into the table at $9124 (6 bytes a tune: two voices, each a script address and a priority), through $89D5, which leaves it alone if another start is pending.
Start tune A from the table at $9124 at once, both voices through $89E5.

Two-voice sound and tune list, 6 bytes each: script address and priority for one voice, then for another. Offsets 0, 6, 12 and 18 are the four end-of-level tunes ($9C46 picks one at random); 24 Jumpman's death; 30 the start of a level; 36 the game over ($A777); 42 the ending after level 12 ($BF6A); 48 the end of the high-score screen ($A90F); 54 and 60 the title tune (three voices: $9472, $94D4 and $9534, and the empty script at $916C); 66 silence.
The tunes' first voice script address, high byte, read as $9125+X.
The tunes' first voice priority.
The tunes' second voice script address, low byte.
The tunes' second voice script address, high byte.
The tunes' second voice priority.
The end of the tune table: offset 66, silence, both voices pointing at the empty script $916C with priority 0.
The empty sound script, a lone $FF: unused voices and the silence entry point here.
End-of-level tune 1 (offset 0 of $9124), first voice: 16 notes, 320 frames, pulse wave.
End-of-level tune 1, second voice: 16 notes, 320 frames.
End-of-level tune 2 (offset 6), first voice: 12 notes, 258 frames.
End-of-level tune 2, second voice: 11 notes, 260 frames.
End-of-level tune 3 (offset 12), first voice: 9 notes, 368 frames.
End-of-level tune 3, second voice: 16 notes, 368 frames.
End-of-level tune 4 (offset 18), first voice: 15 notes, 308 frames.
End-of-level tune 4, second voice: 10 notes, 306 frames.
Jumpman's death tune (offset 24), first voice: 11 notes, 256 frames.
Jumpman's death tune, second voice: 16 notes, 256 frames, with a shorter release.
The start-of-level tune (offset 30), first voice: 21 notes, 240 frames.
The start-of-level tune, second voice: 11 notes, 240 frames.
The game-over tune (offset 36, played by $A777 as the spiral finishes), first voice: 15 notes, 256 frames.
The game-over tune, second voice: 17 notes, 256 frames.
The ending tune after level 12 (offset 42), first voice: 37 notes, 512 frames.
The ending tune, second voice: 29 notes, 512 frames.
The tune after the high-score table (offset 48, $A90F), first voice: 17 notes, 256 frames.
The tune after the high-score table, second voice: 13 notes, 256 frames.
The title tune (offsets 54 and 60), first voice: 41 notes, 832 frames.
The title tune, second voice: 40 notes, 1152 frames, so it runs on past the others.
The title tune, third voice: 26 notes, 832 frames, switching its envelope back and forth between notes.

The title screen. Text screen on, the lines of $8DE2 printed, player records reset ($98DD), the little Jumpman and the bar sprite placed ($975E) and the title task ($9686) started. Waits for a key 1-4 for the number of players, then for each player a key 1-8 for the speed, kept at $0A06 in that player's record and shown on the screen, a blip for each key. Then the first turn: player index 4, level $FF (so the next level is level 1), to $9974.

Task on the title: every other frame cycles the colours of the two rainbow bars in colour RAM and of the second sprite; copies the bitmap screen's sprite pointers to the text screen's. While no key has been chosen it plays the title tune when the voices fall silent, and moves the little Jumpman along the bar by the steps of $978A.
Step the little Jumpman: each step of $978A gives a frame mask, an animation mask, X step (16 bits), first shape, a count of moves and a Y step.
Sprite set-ups for the title (for $8CE1): sprite 7 at X $28, Y $C2, shape $CA, colour 2; sprite 1 at X $70, Y $62, shape $A1, colour 2; end.
The blip for each key pressed on the title, a sound script.
The sound after the number of players is chosen, a sound script.
The little Jumpman's moves on the title, 7 bytes each (frame mask, animation mask, X step low and high, first shape, number of moves, Y step), read by $972D; a 0 ends the run.
The title run's second field: the animation mask.
The title run's third field: the X step, low byte.
The title run's fourth field: the X step, high byte.
The title run's fifth field: the first shape.
The title run's sixth field: the number of moves.
The title run's seventh field: the Y step; then the next move's fields.
The RTS the floor probe branches to when Jumpman is out of its range; the title run's table ends just before it.

Read the bitmap around Jumpman (sprite 0, X at $70/$78, Y at $80) through the colour-set table at $1400. $09A8 and $09A9 start from the level's extra bits at $09D1 and $09D2; then $09A8 gets every colour in the 10 lines his body covers, three bytes wide, and $09A9 every colour in the line under his feet. Does nothing more when he is above line $32, below line $FA or right of the playfield. The movement code decides floor, ladder and rope from these two sets.
AND masks that keep the pixels of a bitmap byte under Jumpman, by his X position within the byte, for the three bytes his body covers ($98AD) and his feet ($98BD).
The body masks for the second bitmap byte under Jumpman, by his position in the first.
The body masks for the third bitmap byte under Jumpman.
The feet masks for the first bitmap byte under Jumpman's feet.
The feet masks for the second bitmap byte.
The feet masks for the third bitmap byte.
Fill the four player records at $0A00 (8 bytes each) from $996C, read backwards: score 0 (three bytes), next extra life at 7,500 ($1D4C), level byte 0, speed 0 and four lives.
Copy the player in play ($0A28-$0A2F) back into record $09AB at $0A00.
Copy record $09AB from $0A00 into the player in play at $0A28-$0A2F: score $0A28-$0A2A, next extra life $0A2B-$0A2D, speed $0A2E, lives $0A2F ($FF when the player is out).
Save the player in play and pass to the next one who still has lives, wrapping round to the first; after the last player the level moves on ($09C3). When every player is out, $09C2 is set.
The byte before the stored player record: reset_players reads $996B+X for X 8 down to 1.
One player record, stored backwards: lives 4, speed 0, a spare byte, 7,500 for the first extra life, score 0.

Between turns. A check of $B2 and $B3, which the loader leaves at 0: if they add up to $3F the machine locks up (interrupts off). Then the next player ($9922): with nobody left, a cold start ($8009); after the last player, the next level ($9B1C). With players, a text screen PLAYER #n GET READY! in that player's colour for 255 frames, then the level's picture drawn again. Then the level is set up: its header copied from $0C40 to $0C00, its own start routine called (header $23), the bitmap's colours set, the sprites placed (header $15), the level's four tasks installed (header $02) and the level's own main routine entered (header $25).

Bring a Jumpman on: clear the level's enemy sprites, draw the status bar ($9F75), then materialise Jumpman at the level's start (header $0C-$0E) in shape $BD: his rows are copied in a few at a time, each with a rising note on voice 1. Then his speed from the player's record, the demo input off, the bonus counting ($09BC).

Move to the next level: the counter at $09AA goes up by one; past level 12 (and from then on) a random level 1-12 is drawn instead. The level's 64-byte header at $BC00 + 64 × level goes to $0C40; the screen is blanked, the status line cleared, the action stopped, the colours set, the picture drawn from the header's script ($0C57), the bitmap shown, the border set (header $29), the start-of-level tune played, the level's name written in the status bar for a while, and play begins at $9BD5.

Play a level: a new Jumpman, then $A600 (one pass of the game) until the bombs left ($0C0A) reach 0. When Jumpman dies ($A4 2, then 0) a life is taken; with none left, the game is over for this player ($A710).

The level is finished: the bonus stops, the action freezes, the level's own end routine runs (header $27), the time bonus left is added to the score, one of the four end-of-level tunes is chosen at random, and then for each Jumpman left plus the one in play, EACH JUMPMAN = and the level's bonus from $9EA2 is added with a jingle. After level 12, the ending; then the next turn.
After level 12 (the first time through): sprite 1, the dancing Jumpman, set up from $9EE3, the ending's task $9D2A installed, the ending screen ($BF00), then the next turn.
Task during the ending: copies sprite 1's pointer to the text screen's, and every 16 frames while the tune plays steps sprite 1 ($89) through the shapes at $9EEA.

Level task (the header's third task on most levels): sets $A4 to 1, Jumpman hit, when a movement tick ($A2) comes while $A4 is 0 and $90, sprite 0's collisions with other sprites, is not 0: Jumpman has touched a bullet or another moving thing.

Task while a level's name is shown at its start ($9BBB): every fourth frame steps the colours of the 20 cells under the name ($63A2-$63B5); every other frame moves sprite 1 ($71/$79) three pixels right and flips its shape between $9C and $9D, a little Jumpman running along under the name.

The twelve level names, 20 screen codes each, written into the status bar at the start of a level: NOTHING TO IT., FIRE! FIRE!., SREDDAL. (LADDERS backwards), HELLSTONES, FIGURITS REVENGE, WALLS., ZIG-ZAG., SPELLBOUND, BLACKOUT, HERETHEREEVERYWHERE., HATCHLINGS and HURRICANE.
Sprite set-up for a level's start ($9B8E): sprite 1 at X 0, Y $F0, shape $98, colour 2, the runner under the level's name.
PLAYER #0 GET READY!, 20 screen codes printed between turns; the 0 is counted up to the player's number.
The border colour for each player's GET READY! screen, index 0-3.
Bonus for each Jumpman left at the end of a level, by level number 0-12: 0, 25, 50 and so on to 300, two bytes each.
The level bonuses' high bytes, read as $9EA3+X.
The byte before EACH JUMPMAN =: the level's end reads $9EB9+X for X 25 down to 1.
EACH JUMPMAN = and spaces, written over the status bar while the bonus is counted.
The jingle for each Jumpman's bonus, a sound script.
Sprite set-up for the ending: sprite 1 at X $94, Y $C0, shape $A4, colour 2.
The shapes sprite 1 steps through in the ending, one each 16 frames.

Task: copy the characters of the status bar that changed ($3E00-$3E4F against the copy at $3E80) into the bitmap's last two character rows at $5CC0, drawn from the RAM character set at $2000; at most eight a frame, and only while the bitmap is shown.
Fill the status bar text at $3E00 with spaces.
Colour the status bar's cells, fill it from the template at $A08B, and write the run speed, player number, level number, lives, score and bonus into it.

When the score reaches 1,000,000 take 1,000,000 off (each byte compared on its own, not the three as one number); when it reaches the next extra life, add 7,500 to that, play $A0DB and give a life; then write the score into the status bar.
Write the time bonus ($0C12/$0C13) into the status bar.
Write the lives in play plus one, as two digits, after JUMPMEN = in the status bar.
The byte before the status template: the template copy reads $A08A+X for X 1 to 80.
The status bar, two lines of 40 screen codes: JUMPMEN = 00, LEVEL 00, RUN SPEED 00, SCORE, PLAYER, BONUS, with dividers.
The sound of an extra life, a sound script.

Task: the bullets ("smart" shots), sprites 7 downwards, as many as the level's header allows ($0C0B), moved on every enemy tick ($09D3). A free sprite becomes a new bullet, at most one a tick: it enters at a random point of the left edge, the top or the right edge ($A210) and drifts one way, picked at random from up, right, down and left ($A219), in shape $A4, white. A drifting bullet that comes level with Jumpman, or straight above or below him, turns toward him once at speed ($A225: 3 pixels a tick up or down, 6 across) with the sound at $A231, and keeps that course; a bullet that leaves the playfield is freed.

Where a new bullet enters, three choices: X low ($A210), X high ($A213) and Y ($A216). A Y of 0 means a random Y between $28 and $E1 (the left edge at X 6, or the right edge at X $16A); the middle choice is the top edge, Y $14, at a random X.
The new bullets' X high bytes, one for each of the three entry choices.
The new bullets' Y, one for each entry choice (0 for a random Y).
A new bullet's drift, four choices: X step low, X step high, Y step: up 1, right 2, down 1, left 2.
The drifting bullets' X steps, high bytes, for up, right, down and left.
The drifting bullets' Y steps, for up, right, down and left.
A bullet's course once it has turned toward Jumpman, four choices: up 3, right 6, down 3, left 6.
The turned bullets' X steps, high bytes, for up, right, down and left.
The turned bullets' Y steps, for up, right, down and left.
The sound of a bullet turning on Jumpman, a sound script.

Task: Jumpman's movement, on every run-speed tick ($A2). When he has been hit ($A4 not 0) it only clears the falling and jump state and stops the bonus. During a jump it goes to $A3FD. Otherwise: with nothing of colour 2 or 3 under or around him he falls 2 pixels, and if the next tick still finds nothing he is killed; fire with the stick right, left or up starts a jump; on colour 2 (the green of floors and up ropes) left and right walk him 4 pixels with a step sound; on colour 3 (the blue of ladders and down ropes) up and down climb a ladder he stands at ($A306); a down rope he touches ($A375) carries him down; green inside his body lifts him 2 pixels, which is how he climbs slopes and up ropes.
Walk: 4 pixels left or right, shape $9E/$9F left or $9C/$9D right, the step sound every other tick.
On a ladder colour: shape $94, and up or down moves him if he is at a ladder.

Is Jumpman at a ladder? His X (in double pixels, less 12) is compared with the eight ladder positions in the level's header ($0C32-$0C39): within 2 to the left or 3 to the right, he is moved onto the ladder and the carry is set.
Climb 2 pixels up or down unless that would take him below line $DA, cycling the climbing shapes $94-$97, the climb sound every other tick.
A down rope: colour 3 at a rope position of the header ($A375) carries him down 2 pixels a tick in shapes $92/$93.
Is Jumpman's X (in double pixels, less 12) exactly one of the six down-rope positions in the level's header ($0C3A-$0C3F)? Carry set if so.
Colour 2 in his body and no colour 3: move him up 2 pixels (slopes and up ropes), in the climbing shape if he was standing.

Fire: right jumps right (shape $98, 4 pixels a step), left jumps left (shape $99), up jumps straight up (shape $94); fire alone or with down does nothing. The jump sound plays and the jump count $092C starts.

One step of a jump: the step's Y change and whether to move across come from $A492; from the eighth step on, $A444 looks for somewhere to land. Below line $DE he dies. After 22 steps the jump ends wherever he is, and the fall rule takes over.
Landed: end the jump and walk on from here.
During the second half of a jump: green under or around Jumpman ends the jump; blue ends it only if he is at a ladder ($A306) or a down rope ($A375), or already in the climbing shape.
The climbing sound, a sound script.
The walking sound, a sound script.
The jump sound, a sound script (its last byte, $FF at $A493, also stands at the start of the jump table).
The jump path's sideways flags, read as $A492+X with X twice the jump step (the first step reads $A494).
The jump path's Y changes, read as $A493+X.
A jump's 22 steps, two bytes each: move across or not (4 or 0), then the Y change: up 2 for six steps, three level steps, then down 2 for the rest, moving across on 12 of the 22 steps.

Task: Jumpman's death, on run-speed ticks once he has been hit ($A4 1). At the first tick he takes a random shape from $91-$98, the death sound starts and he moves at speed 2. He then drops 2 pixels a tick, with a falling note on voice 3 that sinks as he goes lower, until his body meets green; there he bounces (the 11 steps of $A5E8) left, right or straight up at random, tumbling through shapes $A0-$A3, and drops again. Below line $DE he is dead ($A4 2): the death tune plays at speed 4 with his shape flickering, and when it ends he is taken off and $A4 is cleared.
The sound when Jumpman is hit, and again at each bounce, a sound script.

A dying Jumpman's bounce, 11 steps of two bytes: the Y change, then whether to move across (1) or not (0): up 2 twice, level, then down 2 for eight steps. Read with the step number doubled, so the first byte ($A5E8, the $02 that ends the sound before it) is never a move.
The death bounce's move-across flags, read as $A5E9+X.

Called on every pass of the level loop. When Jumpman's body covers colour 1 (orange, the bombs), turns his position into a cell code (X and Y in 32-pixel steps, shifted by the header's $0F and $10) and looks it up in the level's bomb list (header $1B: code, action; $FF ends). Found: the bomb's drawing position from the list at header $19 goes to $09CD/$09CE, the defuse sound plays, the action's high nibble draws a change to the level (a script from the list at header $1D) and its low nibble calls a routine (the list at header $1F); the header's per-bomb routine (header $21) runs; the header's points ($0C11, 100) are added; the bomb is wiped by drawing the blank shape at $8F69 through the small script at $09CA; the status bar is redrawn; one bomb fewer is left ($0C0A); and it waits until his body no longer covers orange.

The routine list's address is read from header $1F as its low byte and, because the high byte at header $20 is stored into $26 instead of $25, from header $1A as its high byte: right only when the two high bytes are equal.
The sound of a bomb defused, a sound script.

A player's last Jumpman is gone. All sprites behind the picture, then a spiral of solid colour wound in from the edges of the bitmap ($A920); the game-over tune; the text screen with TOTAL SCORE: and the score; then the high-score table. A score that beats a line of the table moves the lines below it down one and goes in with the name ddd; the table is shown (***HIGH SCORES.*** and 20 lines), the new line lit in cyan, and three letters are chosen with the stick up and down from $A96A, fire taking each with a blip. Then the end-of-game tune, a wait of 128 frames, and the next turn.
The spiral wipe's arms: how many 8-byte cells each arm fills, one byte per arm, a 0 ending the list.

The step from one cell to the next for each arm, low bytes ($A938) and high bytes ($A951): 8 (right), $140 (down a row), -8 (left) and -$140 (up a row), round and round. Each arm is drawn from both ends of the bitmap at once, the second pointer stepping the opposite way.
